# FirmwareLiberator

> Converts Sonoff smart devices from their stock eWeLink firmware to Tasmota, ESPHome or OpenBeken over Wi-Fi: no soldering and no opening the device. Free and open source, it runs on Linux, macOS and Windows, walks you through every step, and can put Sonoff's own firmware back.

You start it by pasting one line into a terminal; the front page has the line for each system. Each device's status says how far it is proven: Proven means a real one has been converted and reported; Testers wanted means it converts in the emulator, or was added from its official update file and a published pin map, and no real one has been reported yet; Not ready yet means the tool does not convert it yet.

## Devices

- [Sonoff S60](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/sonoff-s60): Proven. Converts to Tasmota or ESPHome. A smart plug with a power meter: models S60TPG (UK) and S60TPF (EU).
- [Sonoff S61](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/sonoff-s61): Testers wanted. Converts to OpenBeken or ESPHome. A smart plug with a power meter (iPlug Gen2): model S61STPF (EU).
- [Sonoff POW Elite 16A](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/sonoff-pow-elite): Testers wanted. Converts to Tasmota or ESPHome. A DIN-rail power meter and switch with a display: model POWR316D, not the 20 A POWR320D.
- [Sonoff POW Ring](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/sonoff-powct): Testers wanted. Converts to Tasmota or ESPHome. A clamp-on energy meter and switch with a display: model POWCT.
- [Sonoff TH Elite 20A](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/sonoff-th-elite): Testers wanted. Converts to Tasmota or ESPHome. A thermostat switch with a sensor socket and a display: model THR320D, not the THR316D.
- [Sonoff Dual R3](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/sonoff-dualr3): Testers wanted. Converts to Tasmota or ESPHome. A two-channel inline switch with a power meter: models DUALR3 and DUALR3 Lite.
- [Sonoff Basic Gen5](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/sonoff-basic-1gs): Testers wanted. Converts to OpenBeken or ESPHome. An inline switch: model BASIC-1GS, not the DIN-rail BASIC-1GSP.
- [Sonoff NSPanel](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/not-ready-yet/sonoff-nspanel): Not ready yet. A wall panel with a touch screen and two relays.
- [Sonoff BASICR4](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/sonoff-basicr4): Testers wanted. Converts to Tasmota or ESPHome. An inline switch: model BASICR4.
- [Sonoff MINI Extreme](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/not-ready-yet/sonoff-minir4): Not ready yet. An inline switch: model MINIR4, not the Matter MINIR4M, which cannot be converted.
- [Sonoff M5 1-gang](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/not-ready-yet/sonoff-m5-1c): Not ready yet. A wall switch: model M5-1C, not the Matter version, whose part number ends in W.
- [Sonoff M5 2-gang](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/not-ready-yet/sonoff-m5-2c): Not ready yet. A wall switch: model M5-2C, not the Matter version, whose part number ends in W.
- [Sonoff M5 3-gang](https://firmwareliberator.com/devices/not-ready-yet/sonoff-m5-3c): Not ready yet. A wall switch: model M5-3C, not the Matter version, whose part number ends in W.

## Start here

- [Front page](https://firmwareliberator.com/): what the tool does, what you need, and the one line that starts it
- [What happens](https://firmwareliberator.com/docs/what-happens): each stage of a conversion, for someone deciding whether to run one
- [Troubleshooting](https://firmwareliberator.com/docs/troubleshooting): problems met in practice, and their fixes

## After converting

- [Home Assistant adoption](https://firmwareliberator.com/docs/home-assistant-adoption): adding a device converted to ESPHome to Home Assistant
- [Updating firmware](https://firmwareliberator.com/docs/updating-firmware): keeping a converted device's firmware up to date
